headline: Transformer models predict microbial and peptide traits from genome sequence and text
label: Learned Models For Microbial Biosynthesis
summary: Pretrained transformers now link genome representations and literature-scale text mining to microbial phenotype and trait prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the application of pretrained or fine-tuned transformer models to trait prediction from sequence and text. MicroGenomer, a 470M-parameter foundation model, is pre-trained on 234.5 Gbp of microbial genomic data and tuned with GTDB marker genes to predict ecophysiological traits. A separate study fine-tunes transformer language models on 3.83M articles to extract a bacterial strain-phenotype network and links those traits to predicted genes. HELM-BERT, a DeBERTa-based encoder pretrained on HELM notation for 39,079 peptides, applies encoder pretraining to peptide property prediction and outperforms SMILES language models on cyclic peptide permeability. What is new is the pairing of literature-scale text mining with genome-level representation learning, directed at phenotype prediction. The items differ in validation targets and output granularity, so the shared element is methodological rather than a common experimental result.
